title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
This is a misuse failure rather than a model failure. A generative system was used to fabricate explicit images of a real, identifiable person from photographs she had already posted publicly, and the fabricated material was then presented as if it depicted her. The person who made it did not need to break into anything, because the source images were already available on her social media account.

The failure sits at two points in the pipeline. The first is generation, where a consumer AI tool turned ordinary photographs into sexual content. The second is distribution, where the material was pushed through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord and Facebook and multiple Gmail addresses, which is what concealed the operator's identity. Catching it would have required either detection of synthetic intimate imagery at the point of upload, or the linking of those accounts and addresses to a single real identity. Neither happened. The victim learned what was circulating from anonymous messages, not from any platform.

What is not established is the tool used to generate the images, the identity of the other users who later produced additional explicit images, and any finding of guilt. The reports describe an arrest and an admission during questioning, and the investigation is described as ongoing. An admission to police is not a verdict.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and spreading obscene AI-generated images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained private photographs from the woman's social media account and used artificial intelligence technology to create explicit morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The 22-year-old victim reported the crime to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after receiving anonymous messages revealing that her altered photographs and videos were circulating online. Police launched an investigation that traced digital footprints across the fake accounts and identified Bansal as the perpetrator. During questioning, Bansal admitted he knew the woman from college and created the content due to personal resentment from past conflicts. He disclosed that after initially posting the content, other unknown users created additional explicit images that he then reshared. Investigators recovered his mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence related to the case, with the investigation ongoing.
title_en: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online
